b: Chris Kies took a trip down I-65 to Birmingham to catch Thundercat on the road behind his new album, Distracted. The bassist and singer brought several of his Ibanez signature six-strings, an Aguilar rig he’s been loyal to for years, and a handful of pedals he’s careful not to lean on. Have a look at some quick highlights below, and tune into the new Rig Rundown for all the details.

Thundercat’s main tour bass was built for this run, matched to the look of Distracted. He says the matte black feels calming and muted to him, which is where he’s at right now, but he also wanted it to be more than just black—he’s a huge Brandon Lee fan, and The Crow is one of his favorite films, from the soundtrack to James O’Barr’s original comic. He figured the timing was right for a tribute.

The Sonic bass was built for a Sonic the Hedgehog anniversary, before a run of dates in Japan where Thundercat wanted to turn up with something special. The games go back a long way for him—he learned to play partly by practicing along to them, and says the music is what kept him playing. He’s still impressed that Michael Jackson worked on Sonic the Hedgehog 3.

Thundercat has been with Aguilar a long time and runs a DB 751, which he calls one of the most solid amps he’s ever used. When they’ve offered him newer gear, he hasn’t been interested. What he wants is power and a lot of sound. Behind him are two 4x10 cabs, chosen mostly for mobility—he’s used 8x10s in the past—with some cosmetic customization of his own.

Thundercat’s board is deliberately kept small. He says effects can cover for not being able to play, and he’d rather you hear what he’s actually doing. The Boss CH-1 Super Chorus has been getting a lot of work lately, including on the last record—he admits it lands somewhere near Duran Duran, then points out those are some of the greatest records ever made. The rest of the board is a DigiTech Whammy, which he uses almost entirely for octaves; a Moogerfooger MF-101, which is all over the Apocalypse and Drunk albums; an EBS DPhaser; an Ebtech Hum Eliminator; and an A/B box for switching between wireless and cable.
